names.note: Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 11. новембар ст. ст., „Св. Урошица кнез Српски.“ — «Св.» is “saint” and not a rank and «кнез Српски» is the `prince` grade `types` keeps with the nation it governs, so it comes off entire and nothing is left but the name the book gives him. It is a diminutive of Урош and the book uses no other form for him; it is NOT folded towards «Урош», which the corpus already keeps for `uros-of-serbia`, a different man — a king who died in 1367 and whom this same book keeps on the Julian 2 December.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 24.11.2025 (11. новембар ст. ст.) — „Св. Урошица кнез Српски.“

attestations.note: The day’s sixth and last entry, THREE SENTENCES LONG, and the only one of them that is not already in some other folder is the myrrh. No `dates`: the entry gives no year of birth, no year of death and no reign, and none is inferred. No `locations`: it names no place at all, Serbia being in the rank phrase and not in the story. `types` is `prince` alone, off «кнез», and nothing else in the heading is a rank. The one `related` row is his father, whom the entry names and whom this corpus keeps under his monastic name.
